Jane —

Quick answers and I've attached two artifacts you asked for: redwood_failover_runbook_v1.pdf (extracted snippets + playbook steps) and rto_rpo_matrix.xlsx (per-region numbers and caveats). See highlights below; attaching full runbook for tabletop prep.

High-level orchestration (automated vs manual):
- Automated: health-based routing, prefix/KV cache snapshotting, model-variant fallback (quantized CPU fallbacks), and staged traffic cutover using our smart routing layer.
- Manual: customer-initiated orchestration actions such as approving DNS cutover when a dependent cloud DB is reporting failover. We can optionally automate DNS cutover for customers that accept the risk.

RTO/RPO (summary):
- Full region outage (warm standby configured): typical RTO 2–10 minutes for API-level routing and model warmup; 99th percentile within 15 minutes for stateful sessions to be rehydrated depending on session size. RPO: up to last 30s of KV cache, application state consistency depends on your persistence strategy (we persist checkpoints to object storage every 15s by default).
- Single AZ degradation: RTO < 60s, RPO negligible for stateless calls.

Session rehydration: we snapshot KV cache incrementally to S3-compatible object storage and keep a rolling checkpoint. On failover we stream the latest checkpoint into the target serving runtime and apply any delta requests from the request queue. For very large sessions we recommend client-side checkpointing to S3 as a complement.

DNS/ALB cutover: we support either active-active via Anycast/Cloud LB or active-passive via DNS cutover. Controlled TTLs and health-probe gating are supported; we typically gate DNS with a health webhook call to your origin.

P0 contact: yes — we'll provide a named on-call for rehearsals and a runbook owner.

Next steps:
1) Review attached runbook snippets and the matrix.
2) Tell us which services/endpoints you want in-scope for the tabletop (e.g., chat API, embeddings).
3) Pick two 90-min windows the week of July 7 and we'll schedule.

Adding a few technical clarifications for Jane and the SRE team to consider when scoping the rehearsal: 

- Warm-standby topology: we run a parallel pool in the target region with preloaded model artifacts and a warmed KV cache snapshot (age configurable). Warm pools consume reduced capacity but allow <10m API readiness.
- Prefix/KV cache snapshot cadence: default 15s; can be shortened at cost of additional object-store ops.
- Consistency model: we treat KV cache as best-effort transient state — canonical data should be written to your persistent store. We can wire post-call persistence hooks (webhooks) if you want eventual consistency guarantees built into your app layer.
- Network cutover: for controlled tests we recommend ALB + weighted routing (shift 10% increments) rather than instant DNS TTL flip to reduce client error rates.
- Dependencies: call out any external DBs, KMS, or stateful connectors; if those are single-region we will not initiate DNS cutover until they report healthy in the target region (manual override possible with exec approval).

I'll also attach a short runbook snippet (in the runbook PDF Michael attached) that shows the exact orchestration API calls for programmatic rehearsals. Happy to walk through it on a call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jane —

Please find an inline runbook snippet below (suitable for auditors). I also attached a short tabletop agenda (tabletop-agenda-90min.docx) and provided our HubSpot event id for scheduling. We can simulate dependent DB failure if you provide either a staging DB or allow us to trigger a simulated health-failure via your LB (we prefer the latter for speed).

--- Begin runbook snippet ---
1) Pre-checks (t-30): verify active region health, confirm checkpoint age <30s, confirm object-store write success for last 3 checkpoints.
2) Quiesce non-critical background traffic (t-15).
3) Snapshot final KV checkpoint and push manifest to S3 (t-10).
4) Initiate partial weighted routing: set target-region weight to 10% (t-5). Monitor 5xx rate and latency for 2 minutes; if 5xx > 1% rollback.
5) Incrementally increase to 50% (t+2) then to 100% after 10 minutes of stable metrics.
6) If a dependent service reports unhealthy: pause routing and send exec-notify; default failback to last stable region. Manual exec override available via orchestration API with 2FA.
7) Post-failover validation (t+30): confirm model inference latency SLA, KV cache hit-rate above baseline, and data persistence jobs completed.

Acceptance criteria per step: each step has a PASS/FAIL gate (metrics threshold file in attached runbook).
--- End runbook snippet ---

RTO if cold start (no warm-standby): expect 25–90 minutes to reach steady-state depending on model size and concurrency. We recommend warm-standby for customers needing <15min RTO.

P0 on-call for rehearsal: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.com) — will be present for hands-on orchestration and can accept exec override commands.

HubSpot scheduling id: HS-9876.

[Attachment: tabletop-agenda-90min.docx (DOCX, 24 KB)]

Let us know two preferred windows and we will lock Marcus and our runbook owner in.

— Michael
